target_customer: Construction suppliers and distributors in HVAC, plumbing, electrical and building materials that extend trade credit
problem: Suppliers chase paper invoices, run credit applications by hand and match payments slowly, which delays cash. Dill moves credit applications, payments, cash matching and collections online and links them to the supplier's ERP.
business_model: B2B SaaS for accounts receivable automation, with payment processing
product_category: accounts receivable automation and payments for construction suppliers

founders.name: Catherine Jiang
previous_startups: A B2B commerce startup (acquired, name not given on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Describes herself as a second time founder. Former product manager at Yelp.

competitors.name: Suppli
competitors.what: Digital accounts receivable platform for construction suppliers

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly standard SaaS and payments work, but integrating with many ERP systems for small suppliers is laborious. The company says its team handles ERP setup and most suppliers go live in 2 to 6 weeks.

defensibility.rationale: ERP integration and payment workflows create some lock-in once live, but the product category is crowded and the idea is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy was found. Other payment and credit firms already sold to construction suppliers.

market_need_then: Construction suppliers rely on trade credit and slow, manual collections. Funded competitors such as Suppli (3.1M seed in January 2023) show active investor interest in the wedge at the time.

branding.domain_note: Uses usedill.com, a prefix domain, not an exact dill.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical, confident and direct, plain language for the trade

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, and the name shares its word with a herb and a crypto token, which hurts search.

pivots.from: Digital invoicing and payments for foodservice distributors
pivots.to: Credit to cash platform for construction suppliers
pivots.why: Not stated. The YC launch post targeted foodservice distributors, the current site targets construction suppliers.

outcome_analysis: Dill is still operating and hiring sales and AI roles per its YC page. It appears to have moved from foodservice distributor invoicing at YC time to construction supplier credit to cash, serving named customers and buying groups. No verified funding, exit or failure evidence was found, so there is no outcome story beyond continued operation.
notes: Seed figures conflict across aggregators: 1.5M in April 2023 with Formus Capital and Punch Capital, about 500K, and about 630K in August 2023. None verified by a press release or Form D, so no round is recorded. A search for outcome news found only unrelated results named Dill. The Suppli article is a different company from Dill. Completeness pass: the $1.5M seed (2023-04-05) is recorded from Bouncewatch, with standout.work also listing $1.5M and adding Punch Capital (unconfirmed elsewhere); other aggregators give about 500K or 630K, so the amount rests on databases only.
